title: Meta Muse Captures 51% Agentic Shopping Share vs Grok
summary: Meta's Muse agent handled 51% of AI shopping orders for the week ending Nov. 22, beating Grok at 24% and ChatGPT at 22%, per Forter Intelligence data.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Meta's Muse agent captured 51% of AI-driven shopping orders for the week ending November 22, 2026, outpacing Grok and ChatGPT.
- Twenty-five percent of Muse users complete purchases through the agent, with average transaction values exceeding $200 per order.
- Meta plans to monetize Muse through transaction fees while keeping the agent ad-free, citing conversion benefits for Instagram advertisers.


Meta's Muse personal AI agent has captured 51% of agentic shopping orders for the week ending November 22, 2026, according to transaction data from Forter Intelligence reported by CNBC. The figure positions Muse ahead of xAI's Grok at 24%, OpenAI's ChatGPT at 22%, and Google plus startup Instinct splitting the remaining 3%. The ranking marks a decisive lead for Meta in the emerging category of AI-driven commerce.


## Market Share Breakdown


Forter Intelligence's dataset shows Muse held 51% of agent-facilitated orders during the single week ending November 22. Over a longer 90-day window ending November 23, Muse accounted for 45% of all agentic orders and 43% of total agent spending. The company did not disclose panel size, methodology, or the precise definition of an agentic order, and neither Grok nor ChatGPT representatives commented on the figures.


The data reflects a narrow competitive landscape. Grok's 24% share places it firmly in second, while ChatGPT trails at 22%. Google's assistant and Instinct, a lesser-known startup, combine for a 3% slice. The concentration suggests early-stage consolidation around three dominant platforms in the agentic shopping space.


## User Behavior and Transaction Value


Meta disclosed that 25% of Muse users complete purchases through the agent, with average transaction values exceeding $200. A senior Meta executive told CNBC the agent integrates with Instagram's saved posts and direct messages, giving Muse a persistent list of items users have already flagged. The executive characterized the tool as reducing friction in the shopping process and enabling deferred purchase decisions.


Mark Zuckerberg noted on Meta's most recent earnings call that the company plans to take a small transaction fee on purchases made through the agentic platform. The monetization strategy diverges from Meta's traditional ad-supported model, though the executive emphasized Muse remains valuable for the ads business by raising conversion rates for advertisers even without carrying ads itself.


## Release Date and Integration Timeline


Muse officially launched on November 22, 2026, integrating directly into Instagram's saved-post and DM interfaces. The timing aligns with a broader push by Meta to embed AI agents across its family of apps. Twenty percent of daily Instagram users save at least one post per day, providing a large funnel for Muse's shopping capabilities. The agent operates ad-free, a deliberate choice Meta says preserves user experience while still benefiting advertisers through higher conversion rates.


## Competitive Context


The 51% share puts Meta in a commanding position against rival[agentic commerce](https://emergent.sh/glossary/what-is-agentic-commerce) platforms. Grok's 24% and ChatGPT's 22% indicate both competitors are active in the shopping-assistant space, though neither has disclosed comparable user or transaction metrics. Google's minimal 1.5% share suggests its assistant efforts have yet to gain traction in agent-driven retail, while Instinct's matching 1.5% reflects a nascent entrant with limited reach.


The ranking is based on a single data source. Forter's methodology, panel composition, and criteria for classifying an order as agentic remain undisclosed in the CNBC report, leaving questions about representativeness and reproducibility. Neither xAI nor OpenAI verified the figures or provided alternative benchmarks.


## What This Means


Meta's 51% share in agentic shopping orders signals an early lead in a category poised to reshape e-commerce. The integration with Instagram's existing save and DM workflows gives Muse distribution advantages competitors lack, while the $200 average purchase value suggests users trust the agent for meaningful transactions. Meta's decision to forgo ads on Muse itself while claiming indirect ad-business benefits reflects confidence that higher conversion rates justify the trade-off. As transaction fees roll out in 2027, the platform's revenue model will face its first real test, and rivals will need to demonstrate equivalent scale to challenge Meta's position.
